summary: Temporary hold on flagged employee departure — coordinate account freeze, forensic image, and license quarantine
description:
Issue summary: HR flagged a voluntary-but-suspect departure for an engineer in EMEA who left the building without returning loaner hardware. HR requests a temporary hold to prevent account/credential changes pending a short investigation.

Background: Employee (internal id EMP-20278) notified manager of resignation effective immediately on 2026-03-09. Manager observed signs that a privileged service account had unusual recent activity. HR placed an evidence hold and escalated to IT/Security. 

Impact: Potential access from unknown device(s) to internal repos and infra. Immediate risk to service accounts, GSuite, and VPN keys. Need to quarantine licenses and freeze provisioning to prevent token rotation that would invalidate forensic evidence.

Requested actions:
- Freeze employee SSO account (do not rotate keys) and disable console login.
- Revoke active refresh tokens for third-party apps but retain logs where possible.
- Image any company laptops still in custody, and request location of unreturned loaner MacBook M1.
- Quarantine assigned GitHub/PR access and suspend service-account credentials created by the identity.
- Place license entitlements on hold to avoid automatic reassignment until investigation concludes.
- Coordinate with Legal for any preservation letters and with Facilities to collect hardware if possible.

2026-03-10 11:20 - Helpdesk (Marco Ruiz) confirmed one company MacBook M1 assigned (Asset TAG: RDW-AC-4782); last checkout recorded 2026-03-06.
2026-03-11 14:30 - Legal (Samantha Chen) requested preservation notice to vendor apps and forwarded data preservation template.
2026-03-12 08:50 - IT initiated remote collection of system logs and suspended broad license reassignments in admin console.
investigation_notes: Auth logs show two new VPN sessions on 2026-03-08 from an IP range registered to a mobile carrier not in regular employee footprint.
Service-account 'analytics-ingest' had token exchange at 2026-03-09T03:12Z originating from a same IP; token scopes appear unchanged.
GitHub audit shows elevated push activity to a forked repo on 2026-03-09 02:47Z; need to confirm whether this was local or via CI.
No evidence yet that KMS keys were accessed; CloudTrail shows no kms:Decrypt calls by the user principal after 2026-03-08.
Facilities team attempting to contact last known address for hardware pickup (response pending).
Employee manager says exit was abrupt and they did not return peripherals (dongles, encrypted external drive unknown).

current_workaround: SSO interactive logins disabled; session tokens left intact for logs. License reassignments paused to prevent automatic reuse. Critical services continue via service accounts with monitoring alert on unusual use.
next_steps: Security to complete network and GitHub audit by 2026-03-13.
If hardware recovered, schedule forensic image with SecOps and Helpdesk on 2026-03-13 morning (do not power on device before imaging).
Legal to confirm any additional preservation steps for third-party SaaS providers.
IT to prepare a list of entitlements to freeze (G-Suite groups, GitHub org roles, VPN groups, cloud console roles) and present for sign-off before final deprovision.
After investigation, re-evaluate for full deprovision or restoration with HR/Legal sign-off.
